problem: Zero-shot open-vocabulary object navigation systems rely on iterative VLM/LLM queries at inference to rank frontiers or candidates, causing latency that hinders real-time robot deployment. Global image embeddings also give weak directional grounding for frontier selection.
motivation: Frontier exploration is an efficient geometric backbone but frontiers carry no semantic information about what lies beyond. RayFronts propagates language-aligned features along out-of-range rays to frontiers, which suggests semantics can be attached to frontiers directly and used for goal selection without large-model reasoning.
key_idea: Repurpose RayFronts by storing direction-binned language-aligned (NA-RADIO/SigLIP) embeddings from out-of-range rays at frontier regions, and select frontiers by cosine similarity to the query embedding as explicit navigation goals, with no LLM/VLM.
insight: Direction-conditioned semantic evidence attached to frontiers is enough for strong ObjectNav without iterative large-model reasoning, giving 78.3 SR at 32.7 s vs 122 s for VLN-Game. For free-form VLN, lightweight parsing plus landmark verification loses compositional understanding: failures are mostly false positives with similar landmarks in different configurations, which a VLM would resolve. No ablations are reported.
method: NA-RADIO dense features: RADIO ViT with NACLIP neighborhood-aware key-key attention (Gaussian kernel) and SigLIP adapter yields dense patch features aligned with text embeddings
Volumetric frontier map: WaveMap log-odds occupancy; frontier voxels (height band, >=3 unknown and >=1 free 6-neighbors) clustered into regions, recomputed every 5 steps

Semantic ray frontiers: out-of-range depth pixels (eroded mask) give rays carrying dense features; each ray is associated with the frontier region minimizing a perpendicular/radial cost, and features are averaged into 30° direction bins per region

Frontier scoring policy: S_m = max over bins of cosine(f_{m,b}, t_q); the top region becomes the goal; falls back to the nearest frontier; visited regions are invalidated; goal tracking uses a reactive local controller on the navmesh
Dense goal detector: max query similarity in the current frame > τ_g=0.14 for 3 consecutive frames, reprojected to a 3D goal, then final approach and STOP

R2F-VLN: spaCy dependency parsing splits the target phrase from landmarks; WordNet synonyms are filtered by embedding similarity; a rotational sweep confirms detection if a landmark similarity exceeds τ_ℓ=0.11

setting.backbone: RADIO (NA-RADIO, SigLIP adapter) frozen; no LLM/VLM; classical mapping and planning
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D with pose; depth clipped at 3.5 m; camera height 1.25 m
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: move_forward 0.25 m, turn_left/right 15°, STOP
setting.simulator: Habitat-sim (HM3D scenes) plus real TIAGo robot
setting.privileged: navmesh from the simulator used for path planning; pose given

numbers.eval_set_note: 60 episodes across 10 scenes (6 per scene) from objectnav_hm3d_v1 validation split (VLN-Game benchmark subset)
numbers.extra: T_max=1000 steps, success radius 1.5 m; execution time 32.7 s

numbers.eval_set_note: 50 episodes across 10 scenes (5 per scene) from vlobjectnav_hm3d_v4 (adapted from GOAT-Bench by VLN-Game)
numbers.backbone: NA-RADIO (SigLIP space) + spaCy/WordNet parsing, no LLM/VLM
numbers.extra: T_max=1000, success radius 1.5 m; execution time 40.3 s

numbers_note: Only Table 1 provides quantitative results; no ablations. Real-robot validation is qualitative (one 'find a sink' run, ~25 Hz).
results: On the ObjectNav subset R2F reaches 78.3 SR / 29.6 SPL in 32.7 s, beating VLN-Game (76.7/28.0, 122 s) and being about 4x faster. On VLN R2F-VLN gets 28.0 SR / 13.94 SPL in 40.3 s, second to VLN-Game (43.7/22.7, 504 s) and about 6x faster (equal SR to VLFM).
limitations: Weak compositional/relational reasoning in VLN: false positives on objects with similar landmarks in different configurations; SR well below VLN-Game
Small evaluation subsets (60 and 50 episodes), no ablations, and reliance on simulator navmesh and pose
Real-world validation is a single qualitative sink-finding trial
